# Rule index: spring

Every rule ID of the spring docs with its headline, grouped by doc. The headline is the rule's first sentence; the full rule (details, values, examples, *Why*) is in the doc. **Before you implement against a rule, read its full text**: search the doc for the ID and read that bullet, or read the doc when the task is centred on its topic. MUST = deviation needs an ADR; SHOULD = default, deviate with a stated reason; no keyword = MUST unless it says *prefer*, *default* or *consider*.

## [Spring Boot: Libraries](../04-solution-strategy/spring-libraries.md)

- SPRING-LIB-01: Spring Boot's BOM manages versions.
- SPRING-LIB-02: Spring MVC with virtual threads (`spring.threads.virtual.enabled=true`).
- SPRING-LIB-03: `spring-boot-starter-validation` is present in every service with request bodies.
- SPRING-LIB-04: Jackson 3 (`tools.jackson.*`) through the Boot starters.
- SPRING-LIB-05: springdoc-openapi 3.x produces the spec (08-crosscutting-concepts/api/spring-openapi.md).
- SPRING-LIB-06: Outgoing REST calls live in `adapter.out.http` and use `RestClient` or `@HttpExchange` HTTP Service Clients;
- SPRING-LIB-07: Resilience uses Spring Framework 7's built-ins (`@Retryable`, `@ConcurrencyLimit`, `RetryTemplate`, switched on with `@EnableResilientMethods`), only in adapters, except the `RetryTemplate` around an optimistic-lock conflict in the application service (SPRING-RES-03).
- SPRING-LIB-08: Mapping code is hand-written (ARCH-MAP-08).
- SPRING-LIB-09: Null-safety uses JSpecify (08-crosscutting-concepts/development/java-tooling.md, JAVA-TOOL-07/08).
- SPRING-LIB-10: Observability uses `spring-boot-starter-actuator` and `spring-boot-starter-opentelemetry` (Micrometer inside).
- SPRING-LIB-11: Messaging uses `spring-boot-starter-kafka` (SPRING-ARCH-12/13).
- SPRING-LIB-12: Spring Data types do not cross ports.
- SPRING-LIB-13: The service ships as an OCI image that meets the image requirements; Buildpacks is the default way to build it.
- SPRING-LIB-14: Awaitility for asynchronous test assertions; no `Thread.sleep` in tests.
- SPRING-LIB-15: Spring Session JDBC (`spring-boot-starter-session-jdbc`) holds BFF sessions on the product's PostgreSQL (SPRING-SEC-37);

## [Spring Boot: Hexagonal Architecture](../05-building-block-view/spring.md)

- SPRING-ARCH-01: New services use the package structure above.
- SPRING-ARCH-02: `@Configuration` classes never go into a separate configuration package.
- SPRING-ARCH-03: Business exceptions never extend Spring exceptions (e.g. `ResponseStatusException`).
- SPRING-ARCH-20: Demo and seed data of a running installation are loaded by an incoming adapter that calls the use cases.
- SPRING-ARCH-04: Core beans are found by component scanning using custom stereotype annotations that make the architecture visible:
- SPRING-ARCH-05: Feature annotations go on the adapter's own `@Configuration`, never on the main class (`@EnableJpaRepositories`, `@EntityScan`, `@EnableKafka`, …).
- SPRING-ARCH-06: Constructor injection only (final fields, single constructor).
- SPRING-ARCH-07: The transaction boundary of ARCH-UC-11 is Spring's `@Transactional` on the application service, on the class or on the use-case method;
- SPRING-ARCH-08: Commands are records in `ports.in` (mechanism for ARCH-UC-05/06: JAVA-ARCH-03/04).
- SPRING-ARCH-09: JPA entities and Spring Data repositories are package-private inside `adapter.out.jpa` and never appear in a port signature.
- SPRING-ARCH-10: The JPA entity is never the domain model; persistence always uses two-way mapping (tightens D3 and ARCH-MAP-02/03 of 08-crosscutting-concepts/mapping/mapping-between-boundaries.md).
- SPRING-ARCH-11: Keep JPA simple: no bidirectional associations or cascades the domain doesn't need, one persistence adapter per aggregate.
- SPRING-ARCH-12: Kafka listeners are incoming adapters and producers are outgoing adapters.
- SPRING-ARCH-13: If an event must be consistent with a database write, don't publish it to Kafka directly inside the use case.
- SPRING-ARCH-14: Third-party SDK types (AWS S3, HTTP clients) never leave their adapter package.
- SPRING-ARCH-18: Every incoming adapter maps the error categories of ARCH-UC-13 explicitly, by their base types in `domain`.
- SPRING-ARCH-19: New use cases start from the `baseline-spring` generator.

## [Spring Boot: Delivery](../07-deployment-view/spring-delivery.md)

- SPRING-REL-01: Flyway runs at start-up with its own credentials.
- SPRING-REL-02: Flyway's connection sets `lock_timeout` and a bounded lock retry.
- SPRING-REL-03: The DML role gets its rights through a schema grant and default privileges.
- SPRING-REL-04: Projects that use `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` (SPRING-DB-06) set `spring.flyway.postgresql.transactional-lock=false`.
- SPRING-REL-07: The pre-deploy variant (REL-DB-01) runs the same image in a migrate-only mode.
- SPRING-REL-06: The image does not carry the release version; the deployment injects it (REL-CD-01).
- SPRING-REL-08: The BFF embeds the bundle through a Maven profile activated by the bundle path.
- SPRING-REL-09: The hashed files are served by one resource handler per URL pattern, each with its own location.

## [Spring Boot: Local Development](../07-deployment-view/spring-local-development.md)

- SPRING-DEV-01: `backend/compose.yaml` defines every infrastructure dependency the service uses.
- SPRING-DEV-02: `spring-boot-docker-compose` is a runtime, optional dependency.
- SPRING-DEV-03: Core services (database, broker) have no Compose profile and start by default.
- SPRING-DEV-04: Images are pinned at least to the major version where the image publishes such tags (`postgres:18`).
- SPRING-DEV-05: Kafka is a single-node KRaft broker on the fixed host port 9092, in the production broker version.
- SPRING-DEV-06: PostgreSQL uses the production major version and a Debian-based image (SPRING-DB-01).
- SPRING-DEV-07: Application settings come from `application.yaml` plus `application-local.yaml`.
- SPRING-DEV-08: No bash or PowerShell start-up scripts.
- SPRING-DEV-09: A frontend developer gets a working backend with `cd backend && ./mvnw spring-boot:run -Dspring-boot.run.profiles=local`, or only the dependencies with `docker compose up -d` when the API runs from the IDE.
- SPRING-DEV-10: The `e2e:smoke` job (REPO-CI-04) runs `docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.app.yaml up` from `backend/`, where `compose.app.yaml` only adds the application image built from the same commit (`spring-boot:build-image`;
- SPRING-DEV-11: The IdP issuer URL is identical for the browser, the app on the host and the app in a container.
- SPRING-DEV-12: Keycloak has a health check and a realm template.

## [Spring Boot: Producing the OpenAPI Contract (code-first)](../08-crosscutting-concepts/api/spring-openapi.md)

- SPRING-API-01: `operationId` (API-CON-05) is set with `@Operation(operationId = "cancelOrder", summary = "…")` on every handler method.
- SPRING-API-02: Request and response records have names that are unique per API version (`CancelOrderRequest`, `OrderHistoryResponse`), or an explicit `@Schema(name = "…")`.
- SPRING-API-03: Required means required.
- SPRING-API-04: Bean Validation constraints on request records are part of the contract (`@Size`, `@Pattern`, `@Min`, …) and show up as schema constraints, so clients validate the same way.
- SPRING-API-05: Every business error status a controller can produce is documented as a problem detail with its possible `code` values (API-CON-05, API-REST-05, API-REST-07):
- SPRING-API-06: Examples (API-CON-05, API-CON-11) are set with `@Schema(example = "…")` or `@ExampleObject`.
- SPRING-API-07: springdoc and swagger annotations stay in `adapter.in.rest`.
- SPRING-API-08: An integration test exports the spec and fails if the committed file is stale (API-CON-03).
- SPRING-API-09: The breaking-change check (API-CON-04) runs `oasdiff` against the target branch, for example:
- SPRING-API-10: Consumers get the committed spec file, not a URL (API-CON-08, REPO-API-01).
- SPRING-API-11: The N+1 check (API-CON-06, API-N1-01) is done for every new read endpoint;
- SPRING-API-12: `LocalDateTime` and `LocalTime` never appear as `format: date-time` in the spec (API-REST-02).
- SPRING-API-13: The exported spec is independent of the test run: `servers` is fixed and the error schema is declared.
- SPRING-API-14: Parameters the server resolves itself never appear in the spec.
- SPRING-API-15: A binary download declares its media type with a `string`/`binary` schema.

## [Spring Boot: REST and JSON Conventions](../08-crosscutting-concepts/api/spring-rest.md)

- SPRING-REST-01: DTOs are package-private records in `adapter.in.rest.vN`, one request and one response record per use case, with names unique per API version (SPRING-API-02).
- SPRING-REST-02: URLs are plural nouns in kebab-case with the version prefix from the version package (`/v1/orders`).
- SPRING-REST-03: Versioning is by version package and path prefix (default SPRING-D7).
- SPRING-REST-04: Decimals and money use the `ApiDecimal` type, never `BigDecimal`, `double` or `float` in a REST record (API-REST-01).
- SPRING-REST-05: Date and time (API-REST-02):
- SPRING-REST-06: Enums are Java enums whose constant names are the wire values (API-REST-03).
- SPRING-REST-15 (implements API-REST-16): Dates, months and enums in query and path parameters are bound as `LocalDate`, `YearMonth` and the enum type, never as `String` parsed by hand.
- SPRING-REST-07: Errors are `ProblemDetail` (API-REST-05/06/07), produced by one `@RestControllerAdvice` in `adapter.in.rest` that extends Spring's `ResponseEntityExceptionHandler` and maps business exceptions from `domain` (SPRING-ARCH-03), including the domain validation exception (400, SPRING-ARCH-18).
- SPRING-REST-08: Optional fields are omitted when empty (API-REST-04):
- SPRING-REST-09: Unknown request properties are ignored (Boot default, API-REST-04).
- SPRING-REST-10: Jackson is configured with `spring.jackson.*` properties first.
- SPRING-REST-11: Collection endpoints are paged with a hard maximum page size, or bounded by a documented upper limit that the query enforces (API-REST-08, API-N1-07).
- SPRING-REST-12: Update endpoints implement optimistic concurrency as API-REST-11 describes.
- SPRING-REST-14: Errors produced by the security filter chain follow the problem-details contract (API-REST-05).
- SPRING-REST-13: Controller tests assert status, headers and JSON body with `@WebMvcTest` and `MockMvcTester` (08-crosscutting-concepts/testing/spring.md), including the problem+json shape of each documented error.

## [Spring Boot: Configuration](../08-crosscutting-concepts/configuration/spring.md)

- SPRING-CFG-01: Own configuration is bound with `@ConfigurationProperties` on records, annotated `@Validated`.
- SPRING-CFG-02: Properties records live next to what they configure (SPRING-ARCH-02), package-private where Spring allows it, and are enabled with `@EnableConfigurationProperties` on that adapter's own `@Configuration` (SPRING-ARCH-05).
- SPRING-CFG-03: No `@Value` in production code.
- SPRING-CFG-04: Own keys use the prefix `app.<area>` (`app.payment.*`, `app.orders.*`), never `spring.*`, `management.*` or `server.*`.
- SPRING-CFG-05: `application.yaml` holds the deployed defaults; `application-local.yaml` the local ones.
- SPRING-CFG-06: Deployments set values through environment variables in relaxed-binding form:
- SPRING-CFG-07: Secrets are read from files mounted by the platform through Boot's config tree:
- SPRING-CFG-08: The database and broker credentials of the running service are distinct from the migration credentials (SPRING-SEC-27) and are rotated by updating the secret and doing a rolling restart (CFG-06).
- SPRING-CFG-09: `/actuator/env` and `/actuator/configprops` stay unexposed (SPRING-SEC-07).
- SPRING-CFG-11: Secret values in properties records have the type `Secret` (CFG-07), a final class in the support package `<base>.config` (not a record, whose generated `toString()` would print the value).
- SPRING-CFG-10: The component that serves the SPA (BFF, SPRING-SEC-08) serves `GET /config.json` from a validated `app.frontend.*` properties record, mapped to an explicit response record (never a dump of the `Environment`).

## [Spring Boot: Data Protection](../08-crosscutting-concepts/data-protection/spring.md)

- SPRING-DP-01: A retention job is an incoming adapter in `adapter.in.scheduling`:
- SPRING-DP-02: Deletion runs in bounded batches, one transaction per batch, repeated until nothing is left.
- SPRING-DP-03: Child tables owned by the person reference their parent with `ON DELETE CASCADE` in the migration, so one delete per aggregate removes everything the deletion concept lists for that category.
- SPRING-DP-04: History, messaging and idempotency stores are part of erasure and retention.
- SPRING-DP-05: Events are keyed by the person's or aggregate's ID and carry personal fields only where the consumer needs them.
- SPRING-DP-06: Retention, export and erasure adapters are tested against Testcontainers PostgreSQL with the real migrations (SPRING-DB-14) as `*IT`:
- SPRING-DP-07: Use cases that handle personal data have a test asserting it does not reach the log:

## [Spring: Internationalization](../08-crosscutting-concepts/i18n/spring.md)

- SPRING-I18N-01: One `MessageSource` (Boot auto-configuration, basename `messages`, UTF-8, `spring.messages.fallback-to-system-locale=false`) and one `LocaleResolver` bean with an explicit supported-locale list and default, both in `adapter.in.rest` or its configuration.
- SPRING-I18N-02: Business errors map to a stable `code` in the ProblemDetail.
- SPRING-I18N-03: `Content-Language` is set on localized responses;
- SPRING-I18N-04: `Locale`, `MessageSource` and `LocaleContextHolder` never appear in `domain`, `ports` or use cases;
- SPRING-I18N-05: Outgoing adapters render emails and documents from templates and bundles using the recipient's stored language, never the request locale.
- SPRING-I18N-06: Validation messages use bundle keys (`{…}` message templates) resolved through the same message sources, and the response still carries `code` per violation.
- SPRING-I18N-07: Bundles are UTF-8 `.properties` per supported locale, keys prefixed by area (`error.`, `validation.`, `mail.<template>.`), managed in Weblate as a second component next to the frontend catalogs (TOOL-I18N-01).
- SPRING-I18N-08: Server-side sorting that users see uses an explicit collation per locale, documented per endpoint.
- SPRING-I18N-09: The time zone is stored per user when emails or reports need it;

## [Spring Boot: Logging](../08-crosscutting-concepts/logging/spring.md)

- SPRING-LOG-01: SLF4J is the API, Logback the backend (Boot default).
- SPRING-LOG-02: Outside local development, logs are structured JSON through Boot's built-in support: `logging.structured.format.console=ecs` (or `logstash` if the platform needs it):
- SPRING-LOG-03: Correlation comes from tracing.
- SPRING-LOG-04: Levels are configuration:
- SPRING-LOG-05: Parameterized messages only (`log.info("Order {} placed", id)`), never string concatenation.
- SPRING-LOG-06: Where logging happens:
- SPRING-LOG-07: An exception is logged once, where it is handled (the REST `@RestControllerAdvice`, the Kafka error handler).
- SPRING-LOG-08: Never log secrets, tokens, passwords, full request/response bodies or personal data.
- SPRING-LOG-09: Logs are asserted in tests only where they matter, with Boot's `OutputCaptureExtension`:

## [Spring Boot: Messaging with Kafka](../08-crosscutting-concepts/messaging/spring.md)

- SPRING-MSG-01: Listeners live in `adapter.in.kafka`, producers and the outbox in `adapter.out.kafka`, each class with `@MessagingAdapter` (SPRING-ARCH-04).
- SPRING-MSG-02: A listener dispatches on the envelope `type`, maps and calls the incoming port.
- SPRING-MSG-03: Kafka settings are explicit in `application.yaml`:
- SPRING-MSG-04: JSON is written and read with Boot's Jackson 3 `JsonMapper`, as strings.
- SPRING-MSG-05: One `DefaultErrorHandler` bean with a `DeadLetterPublishingRecoverer`, an explicit DLT name and a bounded exponential backoff.
- SPRING-MSG-06: Dead letters are counted.
- SPRING-MSG-07: The outbox is a table plus a relay inside `adapter.out.kafka`.
- SPRING-MSG-13: A side effect after commit without a broker (an e-mail, a call to an external system) uses the same outbox shape inside its own adapter.
- SPRING-MSG-08: Consumers deduplicate through an inbox port unless the use case is naturally idempotent (MSG-IDM-02).
- SPRING-MSG-09: Offsets are committed by the container.
- SPRING-MSG-11: The AsyncAPI document is generated with Springwolf and committed (MSG-CON-01):
- SPRING-MSG-12: Kafka adapter tests are `*IT` with the shared Testcontainers Kafka (`org.testcontainers.kafka.KafkaContainer`, `apache/kafka` in the production broker version, `@ServiceConnection`, SPRING-TEST-04/07), awaited with Awaitility (SPRING-TEST-09).

## [Spring Boot: Observability and Operability](../08-crosscutting-concepts/observability/spring.md)

- SPRING-OBS-01: Probes are served on the main port; everything else of actuator runs on a separate management port (OBS-19, realisation a).
- SPRING-OBS-02: Probes stay reachable despite `anyRequest().authenticated()` (SPRING-SEC-01) through one dedicated `SecurityFilterChain` for actuator and the probe paths, ordered before the API chain, in `adapter.in.rest`.
- SPRING-OBS-03: The liveness group keeps its default (`livenessState`) and gets no other contributor (OBS-02).
- SPRING-OBS-04: Graceful shutdown stays on, and the budget is the sum of the shutdown phases (OBS-04).
- SPRING-OBS-05: Kafka listeners finish their current poll on shutdown:
- SPRING-OBS-06: Business metrics go through an outgoing port in `ports.out` (`OrderMetricsPort.orderPlaced(channel)`), implemented in `adapter.out.metrics` with `MeterRegistry`.
- SPRING-OBS-07: Common attributes come from configuration, not code.
- SPRING-OBS-08: Export endpoints and sampling are set per environment through environment variables (CFG-03):
- SPRING-OBS-09: Outbound calls and messages carry the trace.
- SPRING-OBS-10: Error responses return the trace id.
- SPRING-OBS-11: Operability is tested:

## [Spring Boot: Persistence with PostgreSQL](../08-crosscutting-concepts/persistence/spring.md)

- SPRING-DB-01: PostgreSQL is the engine, in the same major version everywhere (production, local Compose, Testcontainers).
- SPRING-DB-02: Flyway owns the schema.
- SPRING-DB-03: `spring.jpa.open-in-view=false`.
- SPRING-DB-04: Migrations are immutable once merged.
- SPRING-DB-05: Migrations are backward compatible with the previous release (expand/contract):
- SPRING-DB-06: Long-locking DDL is reviewed for Postgres specifics:
- SPRING-DB-07: Names are `snake_case`, tables plural (`orders`, `order_lines`).
- SPRING-DB-08: Types:
- SPRING-DB-09: Constraints live in the database (primary and foreign keys, `NOT NULL`, unique, check).
- SPRING-DB-10: Optimistic locking with `@Version` on aggregates that users update concurrently.
- SPRING-DB-11: Entities have no Lombok, protected no-arg constructor, no public setters.
- SPRING-DB-12: Query ports are bounded.
- SPRING-DB-13: Native SQL and `JdbcClient` are fine where JPA adds nothing (ARCH-ADP-13), inside the adapter, with the same tests.
- SPRING-DB-14: Every persistence test runs the real migrations against a Testcontainers PostgreSQL (SPRING-TEST-05).
- SPRING-DB-19: Privilege tests run as the non-superuser DML role, never as the Testcontainers user.
- SPRING-DB-15: Spring Data JPA plus `JdbcClient` is the default.
- SPRING-DB-16: Invariants across rows are enforced in PostgreSQL, atomically (ARCH-UC-16).
- SPRING-DB-22: A rule over a count of other rows locks before it counts (ARCH-UC-16, SPRING-DB-16).
- SPRING-DB-23: `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` is used only where overwriting is the domain's intent.
- SPRING-DB-17: Every adapter query on a table that grows has an index for its filter and sort columns, and every foreign-key column is indexed (PostgreSQL does not index foreign keys itself).
- SPRING-DB-18: Constraint violations are mapped by constraint name, never by message text.
- SPRING-DB-21: Optional filters build their `WHERE` clause from the filters present, and listings of growing append-only tables page by keyset.

## [Spring Boot: Resilience and Idempotency](../08-crosscutting-concepts/resilience/spring.md)

- SPRING-RES-01: Every client sets its timeouts in configuration, with these keys:
- SPRING-RES-02: Timeout tests use a delayed stub:
- SPRING-RES-03: A use case that mixes remote calls and database work runs the database part in a `TransactionTemplate` and calls remote ports before it, outside the transaction.
- SPRING-RES-04: Tests fail when a remote call runs inside a transaction.
- SPRING-RES-05: The Hikari pool is the limit, so it is sized and its wait is short.
- SPRING-RES-06: Remote dependencies get a `@ConcurrencyLimit` on the outgoing adapter with `policy = ThrottlePolicy.REJECT` (bulkhead, RES-CAP-01), always with an explicit value or `limitString = "${…}"`;
- SPRING-RES-07: A circuit breaker uses Resilience4j (`resilience4j-spring-boot4`, pinned, SPRING-LIB-07):
- SPRING-RES-08: `@Retryable` sits on outgoing adapter methods only, and always lists `includes`, `maxRetries`, `delay`, `multiplier`, `jitter`, `maxDelay` and `timeout`.
- SPRING-RES-09: An adapter called from a Kafka listener does not retry;
- SPRING-RES-10: The `Idempotency-Key` header is read in the controller and passed in the command as a core value object (`IdempotencyKey(value, fingerprint)`;
- SPRING-RES-11: The idempotency table is a Flyway migration in the persistence adapter, written with `JdbcClient`:
- SPRING-RES-12: `@Scheduled` methods live in `adapter.in.scheduling` on a class with an adapter stereotype, call an incoming port, and run under ShedLock.
- SPRING-RES-13: Jobs are tested as adapters:
- SPRING-RES-14: Caching uses Spring's cache abstraction with Caffeine (`spring-boot-starter-cache`, `com.github.ben-manes.caffeine:caffeine`), configured per cache with a size and TTL (`spring.cache.caffeine.spec=maximumSize=10000,expireAfterWrite=10m`, or a `CaffeineCacheManager` customizer for per-cache specs).

## [Spring Boot: Hardening](../08-crosscutting-concepts/security/spring-hardening.md)

- SPRING-SEC-13: Every filter chain sets explicit response headers; never `headers().disable()`.
- SPRING-SEC-14: TLS everywhere outside the developer machine, with the versions of SEC-CRY-01.
- SPRING-SEC-15: Request limits are configured, not defaulted:
- SPRING-SEC-43: Numbers parsed from untrusted text are bounded in length, precision and exponent before any arbitrary-precision conversion.
- SPRING-SEC-31: Queries and commands receive user-influenced values only as bind parameters.
- SPRING-SEC-16: Objects are authorized by owner or tenant inside the use case, and a test proves that user A cannot read or change user B's resource.
- SPRING-SEC-17: The JWT decoder validates `iss`, `aud` and `exp`, and the allowed algorithms are explicit (SPRING-SEC-03 sets `issuer-uri`; add the audience validator).
- SPRING-SEC-34: Request records carry only what the caller may set.
- SPRING-SEC-35: A multi-tenant product takes the tenant only from the `Caller` (a token claim mapped by the REST adapter), never from a path, query parameter or body.
- SPRING-SEC-36: An object the caller may not see answers 404, as if it did not exist; 403 only when the caller may know the object but lacks the permission for this action (may read an order, may not cancel it).
- SPRING-SEC-18: Responses never contain stack traces, SQL, class names or exception messages.
- SPRING-SEC-19: Outbound HTTP to a destination that users or data influence is restricted:
- SPRING-SEC-20: No Jackson default typing and no open polymorphism;
- SPRING-SEC-21: Abuse protection by rate limiting returns 429 and sits at the gateway or reverse proxy by default.
- SPRING-SEC-22: Security events are logged as structured audit events:
- SPRING-SEC-23: Deployed environments (no `local` profile, CFG-04) have no debug flags, no devtools, no H2 console, no Compose dependency (SPRING-DEV-02), and no OpenAPI UI unless it is protected.
- SPRING-SEC-24: The BFF session cookie is `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax` (Strict where the flows allow), prefixed `__Host-` where possible.
- SPRING-SEC-25: CSRF protection for the SPA uses `csrf.spa()` or an equivalent handler:
- SPRING-SEC-32: BFF sessions have explicit lifetimes, and the tokens stay server-side.
- SPRING-SEC-33: Logout ends the session in the BFF and at the IdP.
- SPRING-SEC-37: BFF sessions live in a shared, persistent session store: Spring Session JDBC on the product's PostgreSQL by default.
- SPRING-SEC-40: Back-channel logout with Spring Session JDBC maps the IdP `sid` to session ids in an own table.
- SPRING-SEC-42 (SHOULD): Session attributes are serialized as JSON, so live sessions survive a rolling framework upgrade; otherwise the release steps state that an upgrade logs every user out.
- SPRING-SEC-38: The BFF authenticates to the IdP as a confidential client and still uses PKCE.
- SPRING-SEC-26: Uploads are limited and stored, scanned and served so that a file cannot attack the server or other users:
- SPRING-SEC-27: The application's database role has DML rights only;
- SPRING-SEC-28: Kafka in non-local environments uses TLS and SASL authentication, ACLs per service for topics and consumer groups, and no auto-created topics.
- SPRING-SEC-29: The image meets the image requirements as a security capability: OCI, runs as non-root, minimal base pinned by digest, no build tools, sources or secrets in any layer, an SBOM from the build (SEC-CI-03).
- SPRING-SEC-30: Cryptography follows SEC-CRY-01..05 with platform libraries only:

## [Spring Boot: Security](../08-crosscutting-concepts/security/spring.md)

- SPRING-SEC-01: The `SecurityFilterChain`, CORS configuration and the `Authentication → Caller` conversion live in `adapter.in.rest` (next to what they configure, SPRING-ARCH-02).
- SPRING-SEC-02: Authorization is plain code on a `Caller`; the REST adapter authenticates, the use case authorizes (ARCH-UC-15).
- SPRING-SEC-39: `Caller` is a record in `domain`, built in one place per adapter, and never null.
- SPRING-SEC-03: The backend API is an OAuth2 resource server as soon as a non-browser client calls it (`spring-boot-starter-security-oauth2-resource-server`, JWT validated through `issuer-uri`):
- SPRING-SEC-04: Stateless and token-based means CSRF off for that chain; a cookie-authenticated chain keeps CSRF on.
- SPRING-SEC-05: CORS is one `CorsConfigurationSource` with explicit origins from configuration.
- SPRING-SEC-06: Secrets: see SEC-INC-01 and CFG-05; nothing sensitive is logged (SPRING-LOG-08).
- SPRING-SEC-07: Actuator is allow-listed:
- SPRING-SEC-08: Browser applications authenticate through a backend-for-frontend (BFF) that performs the OIDC login, keeps the tokens server-side and gives the browser a session cookie (CSRF protection on).
- SPRING-SEC-09: Whether the BFF is its own component (`backend-bff/`, REPO-LAY-03) or an additional filter chain (`spring-boot-starter-security-oauth2-client`) in the backend is decided per project in an ADR.
- SPRING-SEC-41: Users the product administers are provisioned in the IdP through an outgoing port, never by a second user store with passwords:
- SPRING-SEC-44: A product account is linked to an IdP subject only on a verified e-mail address and only while it is not linked yet.
- SPRING-SEC-10: Every endpoint has security tests for 401 (no token), 403 (insufficient permission) and the success case, with the `jwt()` request post-processor from the `*-security-test` starters.
- SPRING-SEC-11: Authorization rules are unit-tested on `Caller` without a Spring context (use-case tests, London style for the ports, TEST-TDD).
- SPRING-SEC-12: The forwarded-header strategy is set explicitly per deployment, never left to the default:

## [Spring Boot: Testing](../08-crosscutting-concepts/testing/spring.md)

- SPRING-TEST-01: Tests use JUnit Jupiter, AssertJ and Mockito from Boot's BOM.
- SPRING-TEST-02: Each technology has its own `*-test` starter (`spring-boot-starter-webmvc-test`, `-data-jpa-test`, `-flyway-test`, `-kafka-test`, `-validation-test`, `-security-oauth2-resource-server-test`, …) plus `spring-boot-testcontainers`.
- SPRING-TEST-03: Web assertions use `MockMvcTester` (AssertJ style).
- SPRING-TEST-04: Testcontainers 2.x.
- SPRING-TEST-05: Persistence tests run against a real PostgreSQL with the real migrations (TEST-ARCH-04, SPRING-DB-14).
- SPRING-TEST-06: Statement counts are asserted for query and batch ports (API-N1-05), through a JDBC-level proxy (`datasource-proxy`/`datasource-assert`), which is independent of the Hibernate version.
- SPRING-TEST-07: A test that starts a container or a full application context (`@SpringBootTest`) is an `*IT` and runs in Failsafe; everything else is a `*Test` in Surefire (JAVA-TOOL-19).
- SPRING-TEST-08: Keep contexts cacheable.
- SPRING-TEST-09: Asynchronous behaviour is awaited with Awaitility, not `Thread.sleep` (SPRING-LIB-14).
- SPRING-TEST-10: Architecture tests are part of every service (JAVA-ARCH-07):
- SPRING-TEST-11: `@Autowired` fields are allowed in test classes;
- SPRING-TEST-12: An architecture test fails when a `@RestController` in `adapter.in.rest` is not covered by a web slice test.
- SPRING-TEST-13: Integration tests control background work and reset state in one place.
- SPRING-TEST-14: Use case tests share three fakes.
